text: Refining D-0213 after #353's review, and replacing D-0222, which also restated the evidence side that D-0221 records. This is the in-place proof's side of D-0221's exception rule. A proof takes what each trusted contract it reaches says its operation raises from the inventory's exsures, which D-0221 reads from the contract's own bytes, and the contract's stub copies those Exsures with its other statements. So a contract a proof reaches may name only the exception classes the pinned Nagini models, builtins.Exception and builtins.ConnectionRefusedError, which functions and abstractions may read like the builtins Nagini models. A selected function is refused when one of its exception handlers can catch an exception from a boundary call that the call's contract doesn't declare: a bare except catches everything, and a handler must name a class the contract's exsures name or cover. Maps: dict, list, set, str and tuple operations, and the builtins Nagini models, are part of the verifier's trusted model, as in the legacy cores, and need no trusted contract; a trusted contract on one of them is never assumed by an in-place proof, and its backing tests are still required. The full refusal list: an async function, decorators other than Pure, nested functions, lambdas, global or nonlocal, imports in the function, *args, classes, star imports other than Nagini's, attributes deeper than a module's function, a module used other than to call its functions, names bound more than once, conditionally or not at all, a copied statement sharing its line with another, a copied line ending in a continuation, an annotation the input can't bind, a relative import above the top-level package, a non-UTF-8 source, an async application operation, an exception class Nagini doesn't model, and an abstraction that holds more than contracts, reads more than a function may, or reads a name a star import other than Nagini's could bind; besides these, a module that binds the function's name other than by its one def or rebinds it with global; any name Nagini reads as its own (its contract, IO, obligation and thread functions, the builtins it translates, its predicates and the decorators it matches by name, taken from the pinned image's sources) unless it is Nagini's own export of that name, typing's, or the real builtin; a local or parameter named for a call Nagini dispatches by name; Nagini's names imported under other names; a module that writes its namespace with globals, vars, setattr, delattr, exec, eval, __import__, sys.modules or __builtins__; and any staged application source that writes the module's attributes. A dependency operation no contract binds is named for the distribution whose RECORD installed its module, and with none or several it is an unaccounted assumption; either way Nagini doesn't run on the incomplete input. The result's pins name the recipe, never a local image ID, which the attempt records beside them. Still assumed: that nothing outside the staged application writes the module's names, as a dependency, startup code, patching by name as mock.patch does, or reflection could, and Nagini's own model of the builtins it models and their exceptions.
